slides.heading: Catholic Teaching on Creation and Evolution
bullets: Topic: Does the Church reject evolution or require literal six-day creation?
Source: Genesis 1:1 establishes God as Creator of all things.
Core stance: The Church does not condemn evolutionary biology.

slides.heading: Divine Creativity vs. Scientific Method
bullets: God is Creator via divine intelligence, not chance.
The Church distinguishes faith requirements from scientific investigation.
Latitude exists regarding the scientific 'how' of creation.

slides.heading: Humani Generis: Pivotal Magisterial Guidance
bullets: Pius XII allows research on human body origin from pre-existent matter.
The human soul is directly created by God.
Inquiry must not presuppose philosophical materialism or deny creation.

slides.heading: John Paul II and Evolutionary Science
bullets: Evolution is 'more than a hypothesis' due to scientific convergence.
Physical evolution cannot explain the origin of the spiritual soul.
Soul creation requires an ontological leap outside biological scope.

slides.heading: Interpreting Genesis Literarily and Theologically
bullets: Genesis describes theological proclamations, not scientific treatises.
Origen and Augustine interpreted days allegorically or logically.
Time itself is part of creation, not its container.

slides.heading: Rejecting Philosophical Materialism as Science
bullets: Biology explains speciation but cannot prove existence of no Creator.
Evolution does not address human exceptionalism or existential purpose.
Faith insists on the 'why' behind existence and dignity.

slides.heading: Summary: Embracing Science and Faith
bullets: Accept scientific findings about the 'how' of creation.
Insist that the 'why' requires a divine Creator.
Human dignity and soul remain protected by theological conviction.
